faq: Where do the routed requests appear?
In the place each team already works, such as a Slack channel, a Microsoft Teams channel, an email address or a task board. We match the destination to your team habits.
What if a request fits two teams?
We write a rule for it, such as sending to the main owner with a copy to the second team. Anything the rules cannot settle goes to your fallback person.
Do I need a help desk system?
No. A shared inbox, form or spreadsheet is enough. If you do use a help desk, we connect to it and keep your existing ticket fields.
Can the team see why a request was routed?
Yes. The summary includes a short reason, for example billing question, so a team can quickly tell you if a rule needs adjusting.

desc:
AI request routing to the right team sends every incoming request to its owner the first time. Ecom Swift LLC builds a workflow that reads each form entry or email, picks the team from your categories and attaches a short summary.

## What is request routing?

Request routing is the step that decides who should handle an incoming message. Requests arrive through a contact form, a shared inbox or a booking page, and each one belongs to a team such as sales, support, billing or operations. A routing workflow reads the request, chooses the destination using your categories and posts it there with the customer's details.

When the workflow is unsure, it does not guess. It sends the request to a named person, so nothing disappears.

## What goes wrong when one person forwards everything

Manual forwarding makes one person the bottleneck. When they are away, requests wait. When they are busy, requests are sent to the wrong team, and the customer is passed from desk to desk, repeating their story each time.

Wrong routing also hides work. A billing question buried in a sales inbox may never be answered, and nobody notices because no single person sees the full picture.

## How routing improves results

Customers get answers sooner because the first person to read the request is the person who can act on it. Teams see only what belongs to them, with a two line summary that saves opening every message. The sender can receive a confirmation, so they know the request arrived.

Management gains visibility. A weekly count by team shows where demand is rising and where capacity is short. That makes staffing and priority decisions easier to defend.

## What a good routing setup includes

- A clear list of teams and what each one handles.
- Connections to each place requests arrive.
- A short summary on every routed request.
- Customer details passed along so nobody has to ask again.
- Urgency levels, with urgent items marked and sent as a ping.
- A fallback person for unclear cases.
- A shared sheet or board that tracks the status of each request.
- Rules by customer type or region where they matter.
- A reason line, so the receiving team can see why a request landed with them.

## What we do

We start by reading a sample of your past requests and sorting them with you into categories. We write rules in plain language, including what to do when a request fits two teams. Then we connect your intake points to the workflow and set up the destination for each team, whether that is a channel, a shared inbox or a board.

We test with real past requests and compare the result with where your staff would have sent them. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in intake points, number of teams, urgency handling, status tracking and reporting. You do not need a help desk system for any of them.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep team categories few and clearly different from each other.
- Choose a fallback person who checks regularly.
- Decide in advance what happens when a request fits two teams.
- Tell the team what the summary line means.
- Review misrouted requests weekly at first.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a category for every small topic.
- Sending unclear requests to a general inbox nobody owns.
- Hiding the routing reason from the receiving team.
- Routing by guesswork when details are missing.
- Forgetting to update rules when staff or teams change.

## Who it is for

A growing business with one contact form and several departments can stop manual forwarding. A service company with regional offices can send each request to the closest one. A store whose single inbox mixes orders, wholesale and complaints can split them cleanly.

## What we need from you

Send the list of teams with a sentence about each, a sample of past requests and the name of your fallback person. Tell us where requests arrive today. We never need passwords. You add us as a collaborator or limited team user in the forms, inbox and chat tools involved, and the workflow runs in your own accounts.
